tool.help:
Contact domain calling (Arrowhead) ===================================
**hicArrowhead** calls contact domains with Juicer/Juicebox's own Arrowhead algorithm (Rao et al. 2014).
New in HiCExplorer v4: a faithful reimplementation of the real tool's own method, not an invented stand-in. ``hicFindTADs`` remains HiCExplorer's own, independent TAD caller (an insulation-score method); ``hicArrowhead`` is a second, complementary caller using the corner-score / directionality-index method Arrowhead itself uses, for users who want calls directly comparable to Juicer's own.
Unlike the original Juicer tool, which selects a normalization at run time from a .hic file's own precomputed vectors (NONE/VC/VC_SQRT/KR), **hicArrowhead** works the way every other HiCExplorer domain/loop tool does: on whatever matrix the input file already represents (a cool file's own weight column, an h5 file's own correction factors, or nothing).
_________________
Usage -----
Arrowhead slides a window of *Sliding window size* bins along the diagonal of each chromosome. In each window it computes a directionality-index transform and, from it, a block score combining the upper- and lower-triangle means, variances and signs around every candidate corner. Two passes are run: a low-confidence sweep that relaxes its sign threshold (from *Starting sign threshold* down to *Lowest sign threshold*, by *Step size*) until it finds candidates, and a high-confidence pass at fixed, stricter thresholds (*Variance-sum threshold*, *Sign threshold*). Low-confidence candidates are kept only if they are at least *Minimum width* bins wide and do not conflict with a high-confidence call. Nearby calls are then merged and the final list is written in descending score order.
**hicArrowhead** at full chromosome scale, fine resolution (whole human chromosomes at 10-25kb) can be slow: the underlying computation scales with the square of the window size, the same practical limitation the original Arrowhead paper and tool have. Smaller chromosomes or a smaller *Sliding window size* run much faster.
_________________
Output ------
The output is a tab separated BEDPE-like file, one row per contact domain: chromosome, domain start, domain end (domains are square blocks on the diagonal, so start/end apply to both axes), score, upper-triangle variance, lower-triangle variance, upper-triangle sign, lower-triangle sign.
_________________
For more information about HiCExplorer please consider our documentation on readthedocs.io_.
.. _readthedocs.io: http://hicexplorer.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html
